clue.text: Go away-by small boat apparently

definitions.meaning: to leave or depart, often said as a brusque dismissal
a small boat leaves the bank by being pushed away from it with an oar or pole

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share the idea of departing: a curt order to leave, and the shove that sets a rowing boat moving.

clue.text: Father's sailor is well up in rock charts

parts.note: pop is a name for father, and the possessive gives pops
tar is an old slang word for a sailor

explanation.surface: Dad's seafaring friend climbs the music rankings.
explanation.definitionFit: A singer high in the hit parade is a celebrated figure in popular music.

clue.text: Labour EC sceptic has risen to give support

parts.note: Peter Shore was a Labour minister famed for opposing the European Community
something that has risen is up

explanation.surface: A Labour opponent of Europe rises to back the cause.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Shore was a prominent Labour politician of the 1970s who opposed British membership of the EC.
explanation.definitionFit: To prop up a wall or a policy is to brace it with timbers or backing.

clue.text: Open in Dover Town

indicators.note: in tells us the letters are found inside the following words

explanation.surface: Something is accessible in a Kent port.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt actions are done openly, not concealed.

clue.text: Fieldsman who prior to this has an unblemished record

definitions.meaning: a cricket fielder standing next to the wicketkeeper, the first of the catching positions

definitions.text: who prior to this has an unblemished record
definitions.meaning: someone whose record was clean until now is making an initial mistake

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the slips are close catchers beside the wicketkeeper, numbered outward from him.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the position nearest the wicketkeeper; and an initial error by someone hitherto faultless.

clue.text: Sage headgear heartened Victorian mother

indicators.note: given a heart, so one piece is placed in the middle of the other

parts.note: mama is the old-fashioned, Victorian-sounding word for mother
a hat is a piece of headgear

explanation.surface: A wise elder admires the hat that cheered up an old-fashioned mother.
explanation.definitionFit: In India a mahatma is a revered holy man or wise teacher, as Gandhi was called.

clue.text: He caused Egyptians some trouble with sea opening

indicators.note: to trouble something is to stir it up, so these letters are disturbed
the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone gave the Egyptians grief when the sea parted.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads on into the surface: the prophet who brought plagues on Egypt and led the parting of the Red Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical prophet brought the plagues upon Pharaoh's people.

clue.text: Novel description of period of recession

definitions.meaning: a book by Charles Dickens set in an industrial town
a phrase for an economic downturn when life is difficult

explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's 1854 novel of Coketown has a title meaning years of economic hardship.

clue.text: Rare flatfish displaying highest speed through the water

definitions.meaning: a small uncommon fish of the turbot family
the top rate a ship can make, measured in knots

explanation.definitionFit: An uncommon small turbot-like fish; and read as two words, the fastest nautical speed reached.

clue.text: Ban this concoction from the drink list!

definitions.text: Ban this concoction from the drink list!

indicators.note: a concoction is a mixture, so these letters are mixed together

explanation.surface: A call to strike a notorious brew off the bar menu.
explanation.definitionFit: The wormwood spirit was famously banned in many countries for decades, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: Explorer one found in a landing place

indicators.note: found in means one piece is located inside the other

parts.note: a pier is a structure where boats land
taken as written

explanation.surface: A traveller discovers someone waiting on a jetty.
explanation.definitionFit: A pioneer is one of the first to explore or settle a new region.

clue.text: Corporal signs of corporal punishment

definitions.meaning: a corporal's rank is shown by chevrons sewn on the sleeve
weals left on the skin by a cane or whip

explanation.surface: Badges of an army rank, or marks from a beating.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'corporal' switches from a military rank to 'of the body'; 'of' links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Two chevrons mark an army corporal, and lashes from a cane leave long marks on the skin.

clue.text: Definite conditions applied to USA

parts.note: the word for the definite article in English
states are conditions, as in a state of repair

explanation.surface: Fixed terms are imposed on America.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans and others commonly call the United States simply by that two-word name.

clue.text: Groupof nine returned to the joiner's 'joint

indicators.note: returned means the word is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: a nonet is a group of nine musicians, printed here with the space lost

explanation.surface: Nine musicians come back to the carpenter's workshop.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenon is the projecting tongue of wood that fits a mortise in a woodworking joint.

clue.text: Lassoed by drunken Pedro

indicators.note: a drunken man staggers about, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A cowboy called Pedro, the worse for drink, catches cattle with a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: To lasso an animal is to catch it with a noosed rope.

clue.text: The main trouble in which the unwary may find themselves

definitions.meaning: the main is a poetic term for the open ocean

definitions.text: trouble in which the unwary may find themselves
definitions.meaning: serious difficulty that careless people get into

explanation.definitionFit: The open ocean far from shore, and figuratively serious difficulty.

clue.text: The only striker left for the Fifth Test

definitions.meaning: a striker is a match for lighting, and the only one remaining is the final one
in a five-Test cricket series the fifth is the concluding game

explanation.definitionFit: The final matchstick in the box, and the final game of a five-game cricket series.

clue.text: SIS unit is prepared for complaint

indicators.note: prepared means made up afresh, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A secret intelligence team is made ready for an illness.
explanation.walkthrough: SIS is the Secret Intelligence Service, Britain's foreign spy agency.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinusitis, an inflammation of the nasal cavities, is an ailment.

clue.text: Public admitted to the big golf tournament

definitions.meaning: out where everyone can see, not secret

definitions.text: admitted to the big golf tournament
definitions.meaning: a player admitted to the major golf championship called the Open is entered in it

explanation.definitionFit: Done openly means done publicly; a golfer accepted for the British Open is taking part in it.

clue.text: Diner is treated as a member of the club

indicators.note: treated means processed or worked on, so the letters change order

explanation.surface: A diner is treated by the club as one of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: An insider belongs to a group and is privy to it.

clue.text: So much French spirit results in a fit of temper

parts.note: tant is French for so much
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: Too much French liquor ends in an outburst.
explanation.definitionFit: A tantrum is an angry outburst, especially a child's.

clue.text: Implement for punishing back parts

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tool for chastising the rear of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: A leather belt or tawse was once used to beat schoolchildren.

clue.text: Dish of butter given to English family

parts.note: a ram is a butter, one that butts with its head
kin are relatives

explanation.surface: A dish of butter is passed to an English household.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramekin is a small baking dish for one portion.

clue.text: Satirically caustic paronomastic joker

parts.note: paronomasia is wordplay, so the word gives a pun
a joker is a fellow, a gent

explanation.surface: A punning comic is bitingly sarcastic.
explanation.definitionFit: Pungent wit is sharp and biting.

clue.text: Wines fermented for strength

indicators.note: fermenting changes a liquid, so the letters are changed round

explanation.surface: Wine left to ferment gains body.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinew is a tendon, and figuratively stands for muscular power.

clue.text: Does she sprint after men?

parts.note: read literally, a quick female runner chasing men; really a woman of loose morals

explanation.definitionFit: A woman called this is considered promiscuous, chasing lovers rather than racing.

clue.text: Sweet nonsense

definitions.meaning: a soft confection made of sugar, butter and milk
an exclamation of contemptuous disbelief, like rubbish

explanation.definitionFit: A soft toffee-like confectionery, and an old exclamation dismissing something as rubbish.

clue.text: Early bridge mentioned in few histories

indicators.note: mentioned in says the letters appear within these words

explanation.surface: An early bridge appears in a handful of chronicles.
explanation.definitionFit: The card game whist was the forerunner of bridge.

clue.text: Exempted from local tax act about house vermin

indicators.note: about means one piece goes round the other

parts.note: a deed is an act
the rat is the vermin that infests houses

explanation.surface: A law exempting property from rates is passed concerning a home's pests.
explanation.walkthrough: British rates were a local property tax; a derated building no longer paid them.
explanation.definitionFit: Derating relieved a property of liability for the British local tax called rates.

clue.text: A regular drip

parts.note: seems to describe a habitually feeble person, but means a steady flow of drops

explanation.definitionFit: Liquid that falls in small steady drops forms a thin stream, a slow flow.

clue.text: Regret giving Signallers code to the Sappers

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, the army corps whose soldiers are called sappers
Morse is the dot-and-dash code used by signallers

explanation.surface: Army signallers are sorry to pass their code to the engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: Remorse is deep guilt or contrition for a wrong done.

clue.text: I test an artificially fabricated fabric

indicators.note: something artificially made up is put together anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone checks an artificial cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Satinet is a thin imitation satin, a cloth often part cotton.
